management_steps.details: Sudden onset severe, sharp, unilateral 'loin to groin' pain. Nausea/vomiting, haematuria, or LUTS. Ipsilateral renal angle tenderness.
Urine dipstix (haematuria), U&E, bedside ultrasound (check for hydronephrosis/hydroureter), or non-contrast CT KUB (gold standard).
First line: NSAIDs (Diclofenac 75mg IM or IV infusion over 30 mins) if no renal impairment. Opioids: Fentanyl 1 ug/kg IV or Morphine 0.1mg/kg. Antiemetic: Metoclopramide 10mg IV.

warnings: Urgent Urology Referral Indications: signs of infection/urosepsis, acute kidney injury (AKI), bilateral obstruction, obstruction in pregnancy, anuria, or obstruction of a solitary/transplant kidney.
